identity.name: Karbonsteel Engineering Limited
identity.industry: Heavy & Precision Structural Steel Fabrication (made-to-order, "where PEB ends")

summary.oneLiner: Small-cap heavy/precision structural-steel fabricator ("we start where PEB ends") that crossed INR 300 cr revenue in FY26 on a noisy print — an LPG force-majeure, labour migration, the Khopoli exit and ~INR 40 cr of low-realisation labour/conversion jobs depressed revenue, while one-offs (NCLT bad-debt, premature rent/depreciation, Khopoli shifting) masked a ~INR 16.56 cr normalized PAT vs INR 10.51 cr reported. The forward story is the 30k→54k t Umargam expansion (commissioning slipped to Oct), a fast-growing order book (200→350 cr), and import-substitution of China-sourced heavy fabrication, with data-centre (15,000 t MOU) and railways as new growth legs.

one-line thesis: Small-cap heavy/precision structural-steel fabricator ("we start where PEB ends") that crossed INR 300 cr revenue in FY26 on a noisy print — an LPG force-majeure, labour migration, the Khopoli exit and ~INR 40 cr of low-realisation labour/conversion jobs depressed revenue, while one-offs (NCLT bad-debt, premature rent/depreciation, Khopoli shifting) masked a ~INR 16.56 cr normalized PAT vs INR 10.51 cr reported. The forward story is the 30k→54k t Umargam expansion (commissioning slipped to Oct), a fast-growing order book (200→350 cr), and import-substitution of China-sourced heavy fabrication, with data-centre (15,000 t MOU) and railways as new growth legs.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > One-offs distorting the headline: INR 1.65 cr NCLT bad-debt write-off (booked FY25/26), INR 2.4 cr rent (capex delay), Khopoli rundown/shifting charge, plus ~INR 40 cr revenue compression from low-realisation labour jobs + a relationship conversion job. Inventory improved 150→130 days (internal goal 90–100). Steel rose ~25% (50-55 → 65-70/kg), passed on via PV clauses. Volume +22% YoY (incl. labour jobs).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Revenue / volume: ~40,000 t production on an annual basis at ~INR 100/kg realisation (implies ~INR 400 cr run-rate); full 54,000 t capacity targeted the following year (only ~6 months of the new capacity realised in the current year). Long-term aspiration INR 800–1,000 cr (7,000–8,000 t/month) requiring further expansion post-FY27.
Margin (EBITDA): normalized 12–13% near-term; +1% specifically from automation alone ("other improvements beyond that factor"); normalized H2 should have been ~14%.
PAT margin: ~4–5% for FY26; >5% for FY27; aspiration 7–8% at scale.
Finance cost: ~4% of turnover going forward (paid off high-interest unsecured loans; remaining debt 8–11%).
Utilization: 80–90% on the expanded capacity in FY26; Q1/first-quarter utilization ~80%.
Capex / commissioning: 54,000 t expansion commissioning Oct-2025 (revised from Mar; sheds 1 & 2 ~60% done); 1 MW solar (2 phases) online Oct–Nov; next-year capex INR 10–15 cr (automation).
Order pipeline: +INR 150 cr expected to convert around Sep–Oct (approval received, awaiting confirmation).
order book & pipeline: Order book INR ~350 cr (as of May), up from ~200 cr; ~340 cr executable within the financial year.
+INR 150 cr pipeline awaiting confirmation (Sep–Oct); MOU signed for 15,000 t specifically for data centers.
Stated order-book policy: keep ≥500 cr of orders for a 400 cr revenue target (carry ~100 cr over).
300 t single-piece power-plant girders: 1 order already "uploaded", 2 more of similar value under negotiation.
90–95% of orders are repeat business (precision + qualification = stickiness).

Marquee references: ArcelorMittal + another major MH steel co; bullet-train spans (4,500 t; RDSO-approved, one of few workshops alongside Salasar, Good Luck, Zetwerk); Atal Setu / Vashi bridge form-travelers; IOCL/BPCL refineries. Two of India's largest business houses + a major power-plant company newly audited/onboarded (to add from this year).
segment / subsidiary detail: Heavy/precision fabrication — core; 300 t single-piece power-plant girders ("very few in India can do this"); ~70–80% of 34,900 t output was complex work.
Bridges / infra — bullet-train work essentially complete (FY26 contribution nominal — paint/dispatch tail only); monitoring new HSR lines for future visibility.
Data centers — new vertical; references won via project/inspection-team circulation and technical qualification; 15,000 t MOU.
PEB — contribution now ~0%; deliberately de-prioritised (light industry, EPC, lower-value); prefers production over erection.
Railways products — early-stage product development; aspiration ~20% of portfolio long-term as new lines are announced.
growth verticals / optionality: Import-substitution of heavy fabrication that Reliance and others still import from China (Chinese workshops run ~25,000 t/month; India lacks workshops of that magnitude) — the core long-term thesis.
Data centers + railways as new legs; 800–1,000 cr aspiration on 7,000–8,000 t/month with pricing power at that scale ("at 7,000–8,000 t/month you start setting the prices").
Open land at Umargam for further expansion post-FY27 (funded via internal accruals + equity).
6a. moat & competitive position: Precision/complexity barrier evidenced on the call: bullet-train span of 4,500 t requiring ~3.5 lakh holes matched to <2 mm tolerance, designed for 400 km/h; 300 t single-piece power-plant girders; 200–300 t / 7 m-wide / 100 m-long load-bearing members — "very few companies in India can do this."

Qualification / approval barrier: RDSO-approved (one of few workshops alongside Salasar, Good Luck, Zetwerk on the bullet-train project); new marquee clients require completed audits before onboarding — a slow technical-qualification gate that compounds.
Switching / stickiness: 90–95% of orders are repeat business; "no B or C category clients" — top steel producers, refineries (IOCL/BPCL), ArcelorMittal.
One fact, one home: these durable advantages are captured here, not repeated in §5.
margins & cost dynamics: Steel is a pass-through via PV (price variation) clauses — rose ~25% (50-55 → 65-70/kg), passed on almost fully; "without this principle the company would have faced losses" ("we do not speculate in steel").
Non-pass-through cost leakage: LPG/gas, transport, consumables, paint — a fixed conversion/transport portion is only gradually being accepted by clients (impact taken in Q1).
Realisation ~INR 100/kg vs PEB 115–120/kg, but PEB is an EPC contract (not apples-to-apples; Karbonsteel is manufacturing-only). Conversion margin INR 30–45/kg by complexity.

Automation (cutting, automatic beam welding, fit-up centre, blasting machine under installation, future laser cutter) targets 15–20% efficiency (labour/power/fixed-cost per ton); laser deferred until solar cuts power cost (won't swap labour cost for power cost).
capex / expansion (watch slippage): 54,000 t Umargam expansion (from 30,000 t): INR 21 cr in WIP + INR 10–15 cr more next year (first part shed/building, second automation). Commissioning slipped Mar → Oct-2025 (civil construction + labour delays); sheds 1 & 2 ~60% complete — the key slippage to verify.
1 MW solar (in 2 phases): INR 3–3.5 cr (~25–29/KVA); targets >50% power-bill cut, eventually 100% of power from solar; online Oct–Nov. Energy cost was ~INR 25–30 lakh/month.
Post-FY27: further expansion on open land to reach 7,000–8,000 t/month (800–1,000 cr revenue), internal-accrual + equity funded.
capital allocation: Deleveraging: LT borrowings −5 cr, ST borrowings −10 cr; paid off high-interest unsecured business loans; remaining debt 8–11%; finance cost guided to ~4% of turnover.

Working capital: heavy use of non-fund-based limits (INR 80 cr letter of credit, TReDS/MSME bill-discounting, channel financing); post-listing taking customer advances against bank guarantees to shorten the cash cycle and cut interest cost. Working-capital turnover ~2.2x; total asset turnover ~2x.
Reinvestment phase (capacity + solar + automation); ROE guided 17–19% on INR 115 cr net worth; no dividend/buyback commentary.
risks & watch-items: Execution slippage: expansion already pushed Mar → Oct-2025; verify Oct commissioning and 80–90% utilization.

Labour dependence / migration: LPG-crisis-driven migration of MP/Jharkhand/Bihar workers hit Mar–Apr; "everyone back by end-June"; automation is only a partial mitigant (100% automation infeasible for 200 t / 100 m custom pieces).
Input-cost pass-through gaps: gas/transport/consumables/paint not covered by PV clauses; a fixed conversion/transport portion still being negotiated onto clients.
Customer concentration / large-tonnage lumpiness: marquee but few clients ("no B/C category"); revenue lumpy on large single orders.

Working-capital intensity: custom fab keeps inventory structurally high (130 days; goal 90–100); long cash cycle (procure 30–45d + ~90d production + 15–20d paint/dispatch + 30–60d credit + 5% retention received 6–12 months post-completion).
Sole-supplier / force-majeure recurrence: LPG force-majeure exposed single-source risk (now multiple gas sources); one-off NCLT bad-debt recurrence risk.
management quality / tone: Candid first investor call: openly quantified the one-offs, the ~INR 40 cr labour-job revenue drag, the Khopoli exit rationale, and a normalized-PAT bridge (10.51 → 16.56 cr). Tone confident on differentiation, order book and import-substitution optionality; conservative on margins (12–13% normalized, only +1% from automation). Credibility checks pending on the repeatedly-revised Oct-2025 commissioning and the 4–5% → 7–8% PAT-margin ambition.
non-obvious takeaways: Reported FY26 weakness is largely self-inflicted / optical: Khopoli exit cut 5–6k t capacity, low-realisation labour jobs (~30/kg vs 100/kg full fab) compressed ~40 cr of revenue, and capex slippage forced premature rent/depreciation — the underlying franchise (90–95% repeat, 70–80% complex) looks intact.
The data-center MOU (15,000 t) and railway product push are the genuinely new value drivers vs the prior bullet-train-led narrative (now a tail).
Pricing power is scale-gated: only at 7,000–8,000 t/month does management claim price-setting ability — the 1,000 cr aspiration is a multi-year, capex-and-equity-dependent bet.
Solar-before-laser sequencing shows cost discipline (won't replace one cost with another).
ROE math is asset-turn-driven: ~38 cr steady-state fixed assets generating ~300 cr revenue, mostly non-fund-based limits → 17–19% ROE on a thin 5% net margin.

Crossed INR 300 cr revenue; reported PAT INR 10.51 cr (normalized ~16.56 cr); EBITDA 10.86% (normalized H2 ~14%). Order book 200→350 cr. Khopoli exited; team consolidated at Umargam. 54k t expansion ~60% done, commissioning slipped to Oct-2025. 1 MW solar + automation underway. Data-center 15,000 t MOU signed; PEB → 0%; railways products early-stage. Labour normalising by end-June; multiple gas sources secured.

Next Q → check: Oct-2025 commissioning hit/miss; 54k t utilization 80–90%; data-center MOU conversion to firm orders; finance cost down to ~4% of turnover; normalized EBITDA 12–13% & PAT >5%; one-offs cleared from the print; +150 cr pipeline conversion (Sep-Oct).

themes.title: Steel tubes & building-materials capex beneficiaries
themes.need: Domestic capex + import-substitution lift value-added steel tubes/pipes and building materials - APLAPOLLO/HITECH/JTLIND/SURYAROSNI/SAMBHV/VENUSPIPES on structural & SS tubes (solar structures, DC cooling, API), FINPIPE/SUPREMEIND/APOLLOPIPE on PVC pipes, MAANALU on aluminium extrusions, RATNAVEER on SS fasteners. A data-center-cooling adjacency adds margin optionality.
